_note: THE APP CHANGE PLANE (studio-apps.md §14). An app write is never just a write: it joins a change set, the set is CLASSIFIED, and the classification decides where it lands — a scoped commit on the branch you are on (local), or a branch of its own plus a pull request while your working branch goes back to how it was (structural). This corpus pins the pure half: the CLASSIFIER (what makes a change structural — a document added, a document removed, a fan-out past the limit, a protected branch), the POLICY READER (a hand-edited vcs.json cannot widen the plane by writing nonsense: an unknown `push` value reads as the default, not as `always`), the CHANGE TITLE a person reads in the panel and in the commit subject, the COMMIT SENTENCE with its Despia-App / Despia-Change / Despia-Kind trailers (so `git log --grep` answers 'what has this app ever done to my project'), and the GitHub slug reader that turns a remote into the compare link. Single-runner (the toolchain's own plane — the spend-corpus standing: no kernel evaluates it, so there is no Kotlin or Swift twin to keep honest). Runner: packages/cli/test/studio-apps-vcs.test.ts.

classify.name: an in-place edit of one document is local — a commit, not a proposal
adding a document is STRUCTURAL: it changes what the router reaches
removing a document is structural for the same reason, from the other side
a fan-out past the limit is structural — a refactor nobody asked to have applied
exactly at the fan-out limit is still local — the limit is a limit, not a hint
an edit ON MAIN is structural by itself: an app proposes to a protected branch
a project that unprotects its branch gets its branch back — the policy is the author's
no branch at all (a detached HEAD, or no repository) is not a protected branch
every reason is reported, not just the first — the pull request body names them all
one document written twice in a burst is one document, not a fan-out

policy.name: an absent file is the default policy: commit on, push structural-only, pull requests on
a partial override keeps every default it did not name
an unknown push value reads as the DEFAULT, never as the widest one
a nonsense fan-out is ignored rather than obeyed
turning commits off is a real choice a project may make
a protected list of the wrong shape does not empty the protection

title.name: one created document reads as an add
one removed document reads as a remove

commit.name: the subject names the app and what it did; the trailers make the history machine-readable
a structural change carries its reasons into the body a reviewer reads

slug.name: an ssh remote reads as owner/repo
an https remote reads the same
a trailing slash and no .git still read
a token-bearing https remote reads the slug, and the token never enters it
a non-GitHub remote has no slug, so the plane offers no compare link it cannot build
a local path remote is not a provider
